A free and open-source home screen for Android car stereos.
Not affiliated with or endorsed by any car or stereo maker; brand names belong to their owners. Car names and logos are trademarks of their owners and are shown only to identify the owner\'s own car.
OpenRath has no account, no ads, no analytics and no tracking. It never sends anything to its makers.

Crash and usage reports (off unless you turn them on in Settings > Features) stay on the unit for you to share. On a fleet\'s unit, its managed settings can send them once a day to the fleet\'s own address.

Trips, driving score, routes (GPX), fuel and toll logs, parking spot, service reminders, phone favourites, learnt car signals, settings, driver profiles, waterlogging spots and backups. Backups go to OpenRath/backup on the unit\'s own storage. Dashcam clips go to OpenRath/dashcam and are never uploaded. The parking QR code is made on the unit; only the phone that scans it opens the map link.
SENT ONLY WHEN THE FEATURE IS USED
Weather and air quality: your approximate position (3 decimals, about 100 m) to Open-Meteo.
QR codes (parking, trip sharing, UPI split, parking reminder) are made on the unit; nothing is sent until a phone scans one.
Speed limits, cameras, toll plazas, one-way streets, schools, hospitals, bends, rest stops, petrol pumps and service centres: the area around you to the Overpass API (OpenStreetMap).
Accident help: nothing is sent; the paired phone calls your emergency contact. Car documents stay inside the app.
Map: the map area you look at to the tile server.
Routes: start and destination to the OSRM routing server.
Search: what you type or say to Photon. Voice search uses the unit\'s speech recogniser (usually Google).
Online radio: the station list from radio-browser.info, and the stream from the station itself.
Each has an on/off switch at the top of its section in Settings. Messages shown by the ticker are read on the unit and never stored.
